title: Beyond Molecular Structure: Critically Assessing Machine Learning for Designing Organic Photovoltaic Materials and Devices

Our study explores the current state of machine learning (ML) as applied to predicting and designing organic
photovoltaic (OPV) devices. We outline key considerations for selecting the method of encoding
a molecular structure and selecting the algorithm while also emphasizing important aspects of training
and rigorously evaluating ML models. This work presents the ﬁrst comprehensive dataset of OPV device
fabrication data mined from the literature. The top models achieve state-of-the-art predictive
performance. In particular, we identify an algorithm that is used less frequently, but may be particularly
well suited to similar datasets. However, predictive performance remains modest (R2 y 0.6) overall. An
in-depth analysis of the dataset attributes this limitation to challenges relating to the size of the dataset,
as well as data quality and sparsity. These aspects are directly tied to diﬃculties imposed by current
reporting and publication practices. Advocating for standardized reporting of OPV device fabrication data
reporting in publications emerges as crucial to streamline literature mining and foster ML adoption. This

methods.value: Curating a comprehensive dataset of OPV device fabrication data and evaluating various structural representations and ML algorithms.

problems.value: The challenge of accurately predicting the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic photovoltaic (OPV) devices using machine learning (ML) models.

hypotheses.value: The encoding method of molecular structures and the choice of ML algorithm significantly affect the predictive performance for PCE of OPV devices.

evidence.value: The histogram gradient boosting (HGB) model using Mordred descriptors for molecular structure achieved the best predictive performance with an R2 score of 0.61.

conclusions.value: Data quality and standardized reporting are critical for improving ML model performance in predicting OPV device efficiency.

entities.value: Molecular structures of donor and acceptor materials

failure_paths.value: partial: Incorporating device fabrication parameters into ML models Evidence: While including these features did not significantly improve model performance, suggesting limitations in data quality and sparsity.

partial: Using graph neural networks (GNN) for molecular structure encoding Evidence: GNN regressor struggled due to the size of the dataset, but graph embeddings extracted from GNN combined with tree-based models outperformed direct PCE prediction from the graph.

provenance.cross_sdl_notes: The paper provides a structured approach to evaluating ML models for predicting OPV device efficiency, but the reasoning structure is implicit in some parts, requiring inference. The paper focuses on the impact of data quality and reporting standards, which are critical for ML model development.
